newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks steady on select demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks steady on select demand.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose 0.09 percent on Tuesday as some institutional demand for healthy blue chips cushioned prices, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.13 points to 152.26, reversing a two-week-long slide which sent the bourse on Monday to its lowest level since January 5.
"Market weakness...is usually an opportunity for large portfolios to buy stocks that they want, which are usually the important blue-chip stocks," said Ibrahim Odeh, from al-Wataniyah brokerage firm.
Turnover of 500,743 dinars ($707,264) was dominated by large portfolio interest in a select number of blue chips.

Arab Bank rose one dinar to 252 to partially recoup the losses of this week on market rumours its management may not be able to deliver a promised bonus share this year because of a delay in enforcing a new companies law.
Shares in the bank rose as high as 269 dinars two weeks ago on hopes of a bonus share offer after parliament passed a new law cancelling a 15 percent tax on capital increases.

But brokers say the law will not come into force until another bill governing the stock exchange is passed. That bill faces a long wait to be ratified as parliament is dissolved this week ahead of November elections.
Uncertainty about the fate of Arab-Israeli peace making had also shaken confidence on the bourse, often a barometer of sentiment in the Middle East peace process.

Jordan National Bank and Jordan Cement Factory rose 0.04 dinars to 1.92 dinars and 0.03 dinars to 3.63 dinars respectively, but overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 19 to eight. Another 11 shares traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.02 percent to 79.98 points, 4.10 percent down from the start of the year.
